;GHA-23/0012;Agricultural Growth and Improvement For Livelihood Enhancement AGILE;GHA-2059;Food Security;B;2025;30.11.2025;Planned;750 000;0;;2024;2026;Catholic Relief Services USCCB Inc;;4015;Accra;0159;0159.75;0159.75.111;Afrika - nasjonale tiltak;Ghana;MIA;Kamarainen, Mia;;03;;28.11.2024;Catholic Relief Services;Catholic Relief Services;NGO International;I;Project- and programme grant;Bilateral;Project-type interventions;31130;311;Agriculture;30;Agricultural land resources;;-;-;-;-;-;Significant;Significant;-;Significant;-;-;Significant;Significant;-;-;-;The Agricultural Growth and Improvement for Livelihood Enhancement (AGILE) project aims to enhance the livelihoods of smallholder farmers, women and youth living within the Nawuni Sub-Catchment of the White Volta River Basin (WVRB), through food production, improved agricultural practices, finance and market access. Overall impact of the planned project is the increased crop yield and household incomes of farming families living in the Nawuni Sub-Catchment area in the White Volta River Basin.Target Group: The project will target an estimated 3,325 people in six (6) communities (three each in Savelugu Municipal and Kumbungu District) which includes 300 community water user group members (50 in each of the 6 communities), 30 local water committee members (5 in each of the 6 communities), 25 sub-basin committee members, 420 smallholder farmers (70 in each of the 6 communities, including women and youth), 30 Community Based Advisors / Private Service Providers (5 in each of the 6 communities), and 2,520 people smallholder farmer households. The project will also indirectly benefit over 31,000 people living within the six (6) project communities in Savelugu Municipal and Kumbungu District. The project aligns with national and international commitments to climate resilience, gender equality, and biodiversity conservation. It promotes climate-smart agriculture to enhance food security, strengthen resilience, and protect natural resources (SDG 2 & SDG 13). Integrated Water Resource Management (IWRM) improves governance, protects riparian zones, and fosters social cohesion, ensuring sustainable land and water use (SDG 6 & SDG 15). Strengthening market access and inclusive financing empowers smallholder farmers, especially women and youth, fostering economic growth and gender equality (SDG 5 & SDG 8).;Planned theree year project:

column2: which was ran from 2018 to 2021. The new project is adapted to the dramatic events that took place since the inception of the previous project
column3: mainly the military coup in Myanmar and the Covid pandemic. The current project supports Myanmar researchers and students through skills training
column4: mentoring
column5: and joint analytical/research/communications activities. The objective is to build analytical capacity in Myanmar society
column6: including the growing Myanmar diaspora. The project also seeks to support peacebuilding and democratisation efforts and prepare Myanmar researchers in exile and within the country to contribute to rebuilding the country's political system and state. The project is thematically broad and open-ended
column7: but special attention is paid to the challenge of handling climate impacts in the context of a divided society with a weak and fragmented state. It connects Myanmar researchers across ethnic boundaries in Myanmar and with a network of researchers in the ASEAN region and internationally. It also aims to contribute to more informed debate on critical Myanmar domestic and international issues. NUPI will establish a two-level network consisting of junior and senior Myanmar researchers inside and outside Myanmar. NUPI will engage with individuals and
column9: Myanmar organisations that can contribute to the project's objectives. The project directly addresses SDG4 (Quality Education)
column10: SDG5 (Gender Equality) and contributes to SDG13 (Climate Action). The project puts particular emphasis on the promotion of women

column2: which was ran from 2018 to 2021. The new project is adapted to the dramatic events that took place since the inception of the previous project
column3: mainly the military coup in Myanmar and the Covid pandemic. The current project supports Myanmar researchers and students through skills training
column4: mentoring
column5: and joint analytical/research/communications activities. The objective is to build analytical capacity in Myanmar society
column6: including the growing Myanmar diaspora. The project also seeks to support peacebuilding and democratisation efforts and prepare Myanmar researchers in exile and within the country to contribute to rebuilding the country's political system and state. The project is thematically broad and open-ended
column7: but special attention is paid to the challenge of handling climate impacts in the context of a divided society with a weak and fragmented state. It connects Myanmar researchers across ethnic boundaries in Myanmar and with a network of researchers in the ASEAN region and internationally. It also aims to contribute to more informed debate on critical Myanmar domestic and international issues. NUPI will establish a two-level network consisting of junior and senior Myanmar researchers inside and outside Myanmar. NUPI will engage with individuals and
column9: Myanmar organisations that can contribute to the project's objectives. The project directly addresses SDG4 (Quality Education)
column10: SDG5 (Gender Equality) and contributes to SDG13 (Climate Action). The project puts particular emphasis on the promotion of women
column11: and it is expected that half or more of all partners and beneficiaries will be women. Some of the work carried out under the project will also be on gender issues (details to be finalized in cooperation with partners).";

;Colombia (Corporación de Investigacón y Acción Social y Económica (CIASE)): As part of the implementation of the 2016 peace agreement, CIASE plans to facilitate community dialogues to interrupt cycles of violence and foster co-existence among diverse groups. They will design dialogues from a feminist perspective to reconfigure existing power dynamics to assist participants to learn from the past and co-create the future. CIASE will also inform gender-responsive policy for criminal organizations who target women peacebuilders, human rights defenders, and ex-combatants in collaboration with the National Commission for Security Guarantees. ;
